macros.name: changes
macros.doc: To maintain a change history within the file, the \changes command may be placed amongst the description part of the changed code.

macros.name: code
macros.doc: \code encapsulates page or code line numbers in entries generated by parsing the code inside macrocode environments.

macros.name: CodelineNumbered
macros.doc: When you don’t wish to get an index but want your code lines numbered use \CodelineNumbered instead of \CodelineIndex. This prevents the generation of an unnecessary .idx file.

macros.name: DescribeEnv
macros.doc: An analogous macro \DescribeEnv should be used to indicate that a LaTeX environment is explained. It will produce a somewhat different index entry and a slightly different display in the margin.

macros.name: DescribeEnv
macros.doc: An analogous macro \DescribeEnv should be used to indicate that a LaTeX environment is explained. It will produce a somewhat different index entry and a slightly different display in the margin.

macros.name: EnableCrossrefs
macros.doc: The macro \EnableCrossrefs will also disable any \DisableCrossrefs command encountered afterwards.

macros.name: generalname
macros.doc: This macro holds the string placed before changes entries on top-level.

macros.name: GetFileInfo
macros.doc: Define \filedate and friends from info in the \ProvidesPackage etc. commands.

macros.name: GlossaryPrologue
macros.doc: The \GlossaryPrologue macro is used to place a short message above the glossary into the document.

macros.name: IndexInput
macros.doc: an \IndexInput macro which takes a file name as an argument and produces a verbatim listing of the file, indexing every command as it goes along.

macros.name: IndexMin
macros.doc: When the theindex environment starts it will measure how much space is left on the current page. If this is more than \IndexMin then the index will start on this page.

macros.name: IndexParms
macros.doc: Formatting of the index columns (values for \columnssep etc.) is controlled by the \IndexParms macro.

macros.name: IndexPrologue
macros.doc: The \IndexPrologue macro is used to place a short message into the document above the index.

macros.name: meta
macros.doc: \meta which has one argument and produces something like ⟨dimen parameter⟩.

macros.name: OnlyDescription
macros.doc: You can use the \OnlyDescription declaration in the driver file to suppress the last part of your document (which presumably exhibits the code).

macros.name: PrintIndex
macros.doc: To read in and print the sorted index, just put the \PrintIndex command as the last (commented-out, and thus executed during the documentation pass through the file) command in your package file.

macros.name: ProvideDocElement
macros.doc: This declaration does nothing when the doc element is already declared, otherwise it works like \NewDocElement. It can be useful if you have many documentation files that you may want to process individually as well as together.

macros.name: ProvideDocElement
macros.doc: This declaration does nothing when the doc element is already declared, otherwise it works like \NewDocElement. It can be useful if you have many documentation files that you may want to process individually as well as together.

macros.name: SetupDoc
macros.doc: Instead of providing options to the doc package you can call \SetupDoc and provide them there. This allows, for example, to change default values in case doc was already loaded earlier.

macros.name: SpecialEnvIndex
macros.doc: To index the usage of a macro or an environment \SpecialMacroIndex and \SpecialEnvIndex may be used.

macros.name: SpecialEscapechar
macros.doc: The macro \SpecialEscapechar is used to denote a special escape character for the next macrocode environment.

macros.name: SpecialMacroIndex
macros.doc: To index the usage of a macro or an environment \SpecialMacroIndex and \SpecialEnvIndex may be used.

macros.name: usage
macros.doc: The \usage macro is used to indicate entries describing the usage of a macro.

envs.name: environment
envs.doc: For documenting the definition of environments one can use the environment environment which works like the macro environment, except that it expects an ⟨env-name⟩ (without a backslash) as its argument and internally provides different index entries suitable for environments.

envs.name: environment
envs.doc: For documenting the definition of environments one can use the environment environment which works like the macro environment, except that it expects an ⟨env-name⟩ (without a backslash) as its argument and internally provides different index entries suitable for environments.

envs.name: macrocode
envs.doc: Parts of the macro definition will be surrounded by the environment macrocode.

envs.name: macrocode*
envs.doc: Parts of the macro definition will be surrounded by the environment macrocode.
